name: Stripe
summary: Candidates report a recruiter call, a 60-minute practical coding screen, then an onsite of coding, bug bash, integration, system design and behavioural rounds. Questions are reported to be multi-part, work-like problems rather than classic LeetCode puzzles.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.what: Background, interest in Stripe and fit for the role.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen
rounds.what: A practical multi-part coding problem in CoderPad or your own IDE, often parsing and processing records.

rounds.name: Onsite coding
rounds.what: Practical coding with attention to complexity, readable code and tests.

rounds.name: Bug bash
rounds.what: Find and fix bugs in an unfamiliar codebase with a methodical, hypothesis-driven approach.

rounds.name: Integration
rounds.what: Write working code against an API from its documentation, with error handling.

rounds.name: System design
rounds.what: Design a scalable, reliable service and justify technology choices; usually mid level and above.

rounds.name: Behavioural
rounds.what: Hiring manager round on past work, mapped to Stripe's operating principles.

tips: Expect multi-part problems where each part builds on the last; get the early parts working and tested first.
Write readable code and small tests as you go rather than optimising early.
For the bug bash, form a hypothesis, test it, and narrate what you rule out.
Practise reading API docs and wiring calls together with error handling, in your own IDE.
Grinding hard LeetCode helps less here than practising parsing, data modelling and clean code.
